## MMM_ROUTINE_MERGE_POLICY_ADOPTION_001 — task contract

Primary outcome: adopt a bounded routine-merge policy in MMM guidance so
eligible routine follow-ups within approved goals merge on independent Codex
exact-head review plus full required validation, without a repeated owner
merge prompt. Guidance only; no automation service, no approval delegation
beyond the owner decision quoted below.

Status: `authorized`. Execution of this bounded guidance-only contract is
authorized by the recorded owner direction. Correction, merge and PR
authority remain false. Muse-Spark owns the future implementation approach; Codex
reviews independently and must not have authored the implementation.

### Recorded owner direction (verbatim)

> "approved, also fix the process so we dont need these kind of approvals"

This decision covers the bounded process change itself: routine eligible work
no longer needs per-head owner merge prompts. It does not approve merges,
add goals, capabilities, architecture, analytical meaning, or sibling
authority. Owner decisions remain mandatory for all major changes (see
retained decisions). This message conveys the decision for proposal work; it
is not self-approval and creates no exception beyond the quoted words.

### Authority distinction (binding)

- **Task authorization** (owner, Git-durable, scope/branch/gate): always
  required, unchanged. Every task still needs owner-authorized scope.
- **Merge review** (Codex independent exact-head review + evidence +
  eligibility check): always required, unchanged. Every head still needs an
  exact-head review with recorded evidence.
- **Merge execution** (mechanical `ff-only` + post-merge gate + closure): for
  *eligible* heads only, proceeds on the Codex approval record without a
  per-head owner prompt. This is the sole relaxation, and only inside the
  eligibility boundary below.

### Fail-closed eligibility (all must hold; ambiguity → owner prompt)

1. Tier 1 routine only: tests-only, docs-only, or exact-receipt/closure
   commits. No production, analytical, contract-meaning, or package-surface
   change.
2. Within approved goals and the current roadmap phase; no scope, goal,
   architecture, capability, authority, sibling, production/promotion, or
   interface change; all analytical/sibling/capability flags false.
3. Full required gate green on the exact tree (never waived; a required
   category that cannot run is `blocked`).
4. Task execution was owner-authorized in Git; reviewer did not author the
   implementation; Codex records exact-head approval with an explicit
   eligibility checklist in `refs/notes/` and the completion report.

### Owner-retained major decisions (always prompt, never eligible)

Concepts/goals, roadmap direction, new capabilities, material
architecture/contract meaning, authority decisions, production/data decisions,
new analytical contracts or capabilities, sibling writes, interface freeze or
policy changes (including any amendment to this policy), and resolution of
substantive disagreements. Agent agreement cannot expand scope. No future
policy self-extension: this policy can only be amended by a new
owner-authorized task.

### Revocation

The owner may revoke or narrow this policy at any time via a successor task;
revocation takes effect on merge. Any use of this policy after revocation is
unauthorized.

Reuse existing mechanisms only: exact-tree receipts, `taskctl` lifecycle (no

### Prohibited paths and changes

No change to `mmm/`, `tests/`, fixtures, registries, GeoX adapters, sibling
repositories, roadmap goals, package surfaces, or `taskctl` schema/states. No
dispatcher, bot, auto-merge service, binding/occupancy, or monitoring. No
GeoX/MIP scope. No new analytical semantics.

### Defect protocol

If review finds the wording permits any non-eligible merge without an owner
prompt, or any self-extension, stop and report the exact clause. Do not
repair by widening; corrections need remaining authorized budget or a new
owner-authorized successor.
